title: Context affordances labbook — rapid notes and action items
body:
One-week sprint of literature skims + quick mental model sketches. Mostly noisy — throwing down impressions, concrete micro-experiments, and signals to share with Mira/Kendra later. Keep as a living doc.

High-level goal: find low-friction, high-payoff ideas we can prototype on Hosted D1 and Dedicated pools in 2–3 days that could reduce per-token cost or increase effective context without blowing latency SLOs. Focus areas: KV cache pruning, sparse attention variants for retrieval-heavy prompts, and quantization-stability for LoRA adapters.

Conference skim notes (ICLR/NeurIPS-ish session roundup)
- Temporal KV-pruning (paper: "Soft decay for KV caches") — main idea: instead of fixed-size rolling windows, assign decay weights learned from stream characteristics; evict based on marginal contribution to next-token logits approximated by a cheap dot-product sketch.
  - Practical win: aggressive pruning of very old prefixes for long chats with small accuracy loss; notable latency reduction when cache resides in slower memory tiers (NVMe).
  - Open question: cost of computing marginality in real-time vs. simple heuristics (recency + n-gram repetition).
  - Quick idea for Redwood: implement a lightweight heuristic proxy (local L2 contribution estimate using blockwise dot products) and run A/B on hosted traffic slices (non-critical customers) to measure quality drop.

- Sparse attention / block-sparse attention for long context (paper: "Routing blocks by topic") — route attention to a subset of blocks based on topical clustering (cheap projection).
  - Tradeoffs: reduces O(L^2) costs but requires an upfront clustering/projection step per request; works better when context chunks are semantically disjoint (RAG scenarios).
  - Integration thought: use in Dedicated pools where we can batch the projection cheaply; for Hosted API, fall back to dense for low-latency tail.

- Contrastive rerank for RAG-heavy prompts (paper: "Fine-grained rerank signals for LM answer fidelity") — rerank retrieved chunks with a fast lightweight model that predicts token-level hallucination risk. Reranking improves downstream answer correctness using fewer retrieved docs, reducing overall embedded tokens and latency.
  - Action: test with our small T-emb model: compute rerank score for top-20 retrievals, pick top-5, measure F1 on internal RAG eval set. Might reduce embedding usage by 2–3x for some queries.

- Quantized LoRA stability (poster) — LoRA adapters trained after aggressive quantization (4-bit) can drift; solution proposed: small float shadow weights for adapter moment updates, then fused at inference time.
  - For Redwood Optimize: this suggests a new profile: "quantized-adapter" fallback where main model is 4-bit but LoRA lives in 8-bit/float cache. Evaluate memory/latency tradeoffs.

Personal synthesis / heuristics that feel promising
- Workload-aware hybrid cache: hot KV in GPU DRAM, warm KV in host DRAM, cold KV on NVMe with approximate marginality to decide promotions. Most user sessions only need a small hot window.
- Retrieval + block-sparse: use retrieval to provide nice chunk boundaries; then run cheap projection to determine which context blocks to include in full attention. Likely best for long documents / knowledge-base queries.
- Rerank to reduce retrieval width: often retrieval returns noisy top-20; a cheap reranker can reduce to top-3–5 and cut embed cost and token prep time.
- Micro-eval trick: measure per-token marginal logit gain from adding chunk i (compute log-prob diff for next-token on a small probe prompt). Use as gold for offline reranker training.

Concrete micro-experiments to run (priority order)
1) KV marginality proxy A/B test (3 days)
   - Implement blockwise L2 contribution metric in server runtime as a feature toggled by model config.
   - Run on 5% hosted traffic for non-SLA users, measure token count saved, latency impact, and customer-visible quality regressions (we'll use existing prompt-eval hooks to detect regressions).
   - Success threshold: >=5% token savings with <0.5% quality regression on eval probes.

2) Reranker pilot for RAG (2–3 days)
   - Reuse small dual-encoder we already host. Compute rerank for top-20, compare top-5 vs. baseline top-20 retrieval accuracy on internal dataset (task: KBQA).
   - Track embedding calls reduced and net latency. If >10% embed cost reduction with minimal QA drop, consider adding to Optimize recommendations.

3) Quantized-LoRA experiment (4 days)
   - Train LoRA on a small fine-tune with 4-bit base + 8-bit LoRA shadow. Deploy to a dedicated GPU with profiling to measure inference slowdown.
   - Observe stability (loss spikes) and memory overhead.

Notes to self / heuristics for prototypes
- Always measure next-token probability deltas for any cache/prune trick offline before turning it on server-side — proxy stability metric.
- Use canary routing: enable new cache policy only for customers pinned to a canary rollout group in Console. Tie to automatic fallback if user-visible errors spike.
- Keep instrumentation cheap: we already have per-token SLO traces; add marginality probes as sample traces (1:1000) to avoid heavy overhead.

Questions / unresolved
- How fast can we compute a marginality approximation without hurting 99.9% tail latency? Need a microbench on D1 with synthetic streams.
- For block-sparse attention, what's the cost of projection when batching is low (small requests)? Likely unfavorable for interactive latencies.
- What's the legal/ops complexity of maintaining shadow-floating LoRA weights in Private deployments? Flag to Security/Private infra.

Fragments to share in sync with Applied-ML team
- "KV marginality — sketch + perf estimate" slide (one-pager) — target Friday sync.
- Short demo: reranker speed vs. recall on KBQA (not polished) — bring numbers on Wednesday.

References I intend to follow up on (arXiv/blog links)
- Soft-decay KV pruning — arXiv:2701.01234 (linked above)
- Routing blocks by topic — https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05432 (skimmed; clustering projection details useful)
- Contrastive rerank paper — link in slack thread (see linked_artifacts)
- Quantized LoRA poster — internal repo notes + supplemental code in PR #142 (linked)

Quick wins backlog (if experiments succeed)
- Add "rerank-first" recommendation in Redwood Optimize for RAG workloads.
- New Dedicated config preview: "KV-tiered-cache" allowing customer to opt into warm/cold tiers.
- Small SDK helper: sample-and-probe method that computes marginality offline for prompt collections (help SEs debug).

End of dump — clean up later into two deliverables: 1) one-pager for sync, 2) experiment runbook. For now this is the messy labbook.

Otto — 2027-02-20
